# Setting up in RStudio {#sec-setup}

Ten minutes, once. At the end you will have a real book rendering in front of
you.

There are two ways in, and the second is usually the better one.

## Option A: start from this book {#sec-starter}

**The book you are reading is itself the starter book.** Every chapter is a
worked demonstration of the thing it describes — the figures in @sec-figures
are real figures, the applet in @sec-iframes really runs, the maths in
@sec-latex really renders. Copy the folder and you inherit all of it: the UU
house style, a working `_quarto.yml`, a sensible `.gitignore`, and an example
of each pattern you are likely to need.

[**Download the starter book (.zip)**](starter-book.zip)

Then:

::: {.callout-tip}
## Opening a downloaded folder in RStudio
1. Unzip it somewhere sensible and **rename the folder** to your course.
2. In RStudio: <kbd>File</kbd> → <kbd>New Project…</kbd> → **<kbd>Existing
   Directory</kbd>** → browse to that folder → <kbd>Create Project</kbd>.

   *Existing Directory* is the option people miss, because the wizard's first
   screen pushes you towards *New Directory*. It creates nothing of its own —
   it tells RStudio "this folder is a project", writes an `.Rproj` file into
   it, and opens it. Everything already in the folder stays exactly as it is.
   (The zip deliberately contains no `.Rproj`, so the one RStudio makes will be
   named after *your* folder.)
3. Press **Render**. You should get this book back, running locally — nothing
   else needs installing.
4. Now start replacing. Open `_quarto.yml`, change the title and author, and
   work through the chapters one at a time: keep the scaffolding, delete our
   prose, write yours.
:::

::: {.callout-note}
## What to keep, what to throw away
**Keep:** `_quarto.yml` (edit it), `uu.scss`, `.gitignore`, `README.md`, the
`figures/` and `applets/` folders, and `applets/AI-prompt-template.md`.
Keep `make-starter-zip.R` only if you want to hand *your* book on the same way.

**Throw away** once you no longer need them: our chapter files, and every
`::: {.screenshot}` block — those are our drafting markers, and @sec-theming
explains how they are styled. Search the project for `{.screenshot}` to find
them all.
:::

## Option B: start from nothing

If you would rather see a book grow from an empty folder, RStudio will make you
one.

## Make the project

<kbd>File</kbd> → <kbd>New Project…</kbd> → <kbd>New Directory</kbd> →
<kbd>Quarto Book</kbd>.

Give the folder a name. Tick **Create a git repository** if you already know
you want to publish it (see @sec-publishing) — it is easier to tick now than to
add later. Press **Create**.

RStudio opens the new project, and you are already looking at a working book.

::: {.screenshot}
RStudio's *New Project → Quarto Book* dialog, and the resulting folder in the
Files pane.
:::

## Press Render

The **Render** button sits in the toolbar above the editor. The first render
takes a minute; the finished book then appears in RStudio's Viewer pane, and as
files in a folder called `_book` (or `docs` — see @sec-yml).

## Turn on Render on Save

The tick-box next to the Render button. Now every save refreshes the preview by
itself.

This is the single change that makes writing a book pleasant rather than
laborious. Do it before you write anything.

::: {.screenshot}
The **Render** button in the toolbar with *Render on Save* ticked, and the
preview pane updating after a save.
:::

## Source or Visual?

Top-right of the editor pane there is a <kbd>Source</kbd> / <kbd>Visual</kbd>
toggle.

**Visual** gives you a Word-like view — real bold text, real tables, menus for
inserting figures, equations and cross-references — while still saving a plain
text file underneath. A colleague who does not want to see any markup at all
can live here permanently.

**Source** shows the markup. It is faster once you know it, and it is what the
rest of this guide shows.

Most people end up switching back and forth: Visual for tables and equations,
Source for everything else.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Tables are the killer feature of Visual mode
Markdown tables are miserable to write by hand and trivial in Visual mode.
Insert one there, then switch back to Source.
:::

## What is in the folder

| Item | What it is |
|---|---|
| `_quarto.yml` | The book definition: which chapters, in which order, with which theme. **The only file you truly must understand** — see @sec-yml. |
| `index.qmd` | The front page. |
| `*.qmd` | One file per chapter. This is where you write. |
| `_book/` or `docs/` | The finished website. Generated — never edit anything in here, it is overwritten on every render. |
| `*.Rproj` | RStudio's project file. Double-click it to reopen the book later. |
| `_freeze/` | Stored results of code that has already run — see @sec-rendering. |

::: {.callout-important}
## Never edit the output folder
`_book/` and `docs/` are built from your `.qmd` files. Anything you type in
there disappears at the next render. If you find yourself editing HTML, you are
in the wrong folder.
:::
